messages:
dave.m: heads up — paging triggered for routing anomalies. We're seeing hosted customer traffic for acct `acme-corp` assigned into Dedicated GPU pool (dedicated-us-west-2-1) for ~10m. latency + throttles spiking. incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED #INC-2026-314 (sev2) — notified oncall. ops-bot: Pager sent to oncall-l2 (phone). ben: on it, joining. can someone dump the routing decision logs for a few sample requests? alice.k: grabbing logs now. preliminary grep shows policy resolver returned variant 'r14-quant' which is a dedicated-only variant. that should never be choosable for hosted tier. carla_r: confirmed, saw same. sample log:

```
2026-03-15T14:18:03Z request_id=req-0a1b2c tenant=acme-corp route=hosted-default resolved_variant=r14-quant target_pool=dedicated-us-west-2-1 reason=policy_blend_score(0.82) debug=blend_hint:blend_id=blend-42
```

ben: ah — blend_id=blend-42 is a recently deployed routing blend that mixes dedicated variants into hosted fallback to improve p99 latency for big customers. looks like its matcher is too permissive. dave.m: was that rollout yesterday? carla_r: yep, blend-42 was rolled at 02:00 UTC with 5% exposure to hosted requests. it should have had a filter tag `tier==dedicated` but config uses `has_capacity=true` instead. alice.k: here is the offending block from the blend config:

```
{
  "blend_id": "blend-42",
  "match": {
    "region": "us-*",
    "has_capacity": true
  },
  "variants": ["r14-quant", "r12-fp16"],
  "weights": [0.6, 0.4]
}
```

ben: that `has_capacity` predicate is evaluated platform-wide; it doesn't enforce tier isolation. mistake on my end when I scoped the rollout. sorry. oncall-l2: we need immediate mitigation: rollback blend-42 or tighten matcher. any customer-facing impact? dave.m: monitoring shows ~12 tenants had a few requests routed to dedicated. two customers reported elevated latency and one rate-limit error from the dedicated pool (they exceeded per-tenant qps cap). ops-bot: Alert summary: 12 affected tenants, peak extra-latency 350ms, 1x rate-limit error observed, start=2026-03-15T14:18:00Z end=2026-03-15T14:28:00Z (ongoing until mitigated). carla_r: suggest quick fix: change matcher to include `tier == hosted` for the blend or set exposure to 0. ben: can do immediate patch: set weights to [0,0] and flip exposure to 0; will push to routing service now. alice.k: ready to monitor once rollout done. ben: pushed change to disable blend-42 (in-flight rollout flags set to 0). deploying now — rollout-id r-blend-42-disable

incident-bot: CHANGE DEPLOY STARTED rollout-id=r-blend-42-disable initiated-by=ben state=IN_PROGRESS

ben: change applied to control plane, propagation to edge via config-sync. verifying decisions. dave.m: any sign of a cascading fallback loop? earlier incidents had region fallback loops. check for repeated re-evaluations. alice.k: looked at decision trace: request got assigned to dedicated variant once, no retry loop. no loops detected. oncall-l2: I'll keep paging open until metrics look stable for 15m. carla_r: customers impacted list (from analytics): acme-corp, glassco, helios-llc, fenix-ai, orbit-inc, sentinel-data, novahealth, quantworks, apex-saas, steller, blueharbor, solstice — sending notif drafts to CS.

dave.m: short customer impact summary for ops channel:
- root cause: routing blend config allowed dedicated-only variants into hosted traffic due to permissive matcher (`has_capacity`) instead of tier constraint
- impact: ~12 hosted tenants had a small fraction of requests routed to Dedicated pool causing higher latency and one rate-limit error
- mitigation: blend-42 disabled (control-plane flag set to 0) at 2026-03-15T14:24:12Z; edge propagation in progress
- next steps: revert risky blend, run unit test for matcher scope, add preflight validation to prevent cross-tier variant selection

alice.k: metrics trending back to baseline — p50/p95 dropping. oncall-l2: incident severity -> downgrade to sev3 in 10m if stable. incident-bot: UPDATE: CHANGE DEPLOY COMPLETE rollout-id=r-blend-42-disable state=COMPLETE time=2026-03-15T14:26:55Z

ben: confirming decision logs now show no r14-quant picks for hosted requests. sample:
```
2026-03-15T14:27:10Z request_id=req-9z8y7x tenant=acme-corp route=hosted-default resolved_variant=r12-fp16 target_pool=hosted-us-west-2-3 reason=default_hosted_variant
```

carla_r: CS notif sent to affected customers with apology + incident follow-up promise. docket: ENG-INC-2026-314 created and assigned to ben for postmortem. dave.m: add required checklist items: add a matcher unit test, add control-plane validation to block blends that include dedicated-only variants when exposure includes hosted, and create an alert if >0 hosted requests hit dedicated pool. ben: got it. oncall-l2: handing back to eng-sre, leaving channel. :wave:

oncall-l2: time-of-handoff 2026-03-15T14:34:05Z — oncall clear. incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (downgraded) ENG-INC-2026-314 state=MONITORING

carla_r: postmortem owner ben, ETA draft by 2026-03-17. meeting to review mitigation and automation scheduled 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC. end of thread.
